common_name: San Francisco Fuchsia (Carmine-Rose and Geranium-Lake Trailing Fuchsia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants after all frost danger has passed in partial shade in moist, fertile, well-drained soil or potting mix; raised by Victor Reiter of San Francisco and named in 1941 from a cross of 'Robert Blatry' and 'Mrs. Victor Reiter', it later became one parent (crossed with Fuchsia triphylla) of Reiter's 1948 cultivar 'Mantilla'.

directions: Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil or potting mix in partial shade, sheltered from hot midday sun. San Francisco produces single flowers with a carmine-rose tube and sepals set off by a geranium-lake red corolla, carried on vigorous, naturally trailing stems well suited to large hanging baskets or allowed to cascade over a raised bed edge. It was one of the parents used by its breeder, Victor Reiter, in creating the triphylla hybrid Mantilla a few years later, and it shares that lineage's tolerance for a bit more warmth than many older trailing fuchsia cultivars, though it still slows and can drop buds in the most humid stretches of a Gulf Coast summer. Keep the root zone consistently moist and the foliage in afternoon shade, and bring plants under cover well before the first fall frost since cold tolerance is minimal.
